title: Proposed approval of the Detroit, Michigan 2015 8-Hour Ozone Redesignation and Maintenance Plan
pass_4_primary_concern: The proposal needs a clearer, more granular explanation for the deadline reset and the future-year budget support.
pass_5_high_stakes_domain_reason: The notice concerns ozone attainment, maintenance planning, transportation conformity, and the timing of air-quality obligations for the Detroit area, so the public-health and compliance stakes are material.
pass_5_concise_why: The proposal is structurally coherent overall, but the deadline reset and future-year budget logic would benefit from a more granular public record.
pass_5_most_important_consequence: The final rule could lock in a long compliance path and conformity framework through 2040 without as much milestone-level explanation as the attainment path itself.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal uses a reset deadline and adequacy process to sequence compliance after the vacatur, but the sequence is ordinary rather than coercive.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to show the milestone path that connects the deadline reset to actual implementation.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The attainment bridge depends on excluded wildfire days and future budgets, but the preamble summarizes rather than reproduces the full supporting tables.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to put the key tables in a single, easy-to-audit location.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The deadline reset is justified, but the notice does not fully explain why these specific dates are the best remedy rather than a shorter or phased schedule.

evidence.quote_or_absence: without such adjustment, Michigan would immediately be in default of its obligation to submit and implement certain Moderate elements for the Detroit area
The EPA believes it is reasonable to set an implementation deadline that is 4 years from December 5, 2026.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to explain why the selected dates, rather than phased milestones, are necessary and appropriate.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: Basic I/M is described as administratively challenging, but the notice gives only a high-level picture of the build-out effort.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for the milestone sequence that makes the 2030 endpoint practical.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal sets a long-lived compliance path while the conformity budgets and deadline details are still being finalized.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to show how interim review points will prevent drift before the final dates arrive.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The adequacy process and deadline reset are procedural gateways, but they are standard regulatory tools in this context.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA how those gateways will function if the maintenance plan needs adjustment later.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal bundles redesignation, maintenance, budgets, and deadline relief into one notice, which is coherent but still worth unpacking.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to separate the pieces that are legally required from the pieces that are policy choices.
